<think>**Designing decoder predecode**

**Preparing parameterized decoder fallback**

**Verifying N8 loop assignments**

</think>

{
  "candidate_rtl": "module decoder_8bit
#(
    parameter N = 8
) (
    input [N-1:0] in,
    output reg [(1<<N)-1:0] out
);
    generate
        if (N == 8) begin : g_predecode
            wire [15:0] low_not_match;
            wire [15:0] high_not_match;
            genvar p;
            for (p = 0; p < 16; p = p + 1) begin : g_terms
                localparam [3:0] CODE = p;
                assign low_not_match[p] = ~(in[3:0] == CODE);
                assign high_not_match[p] = ~(in[7:4] == CODE);
            end

            integer k;
            always @(*) begin
                for (k = 0; k < 256; k = k + 1) begin
                    out[k] = ~(low_not_match[k % 16] |
                               high_not_match[k / 16]);
                end
            end
        end else begin : g_original
            always @(*) begin
                out = {{(1<<N)-1{1'b0}}, 1'b1} << in;
            end
        end
    endgenerate
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The variable one-hot shift can create deep selection logic and substantial buffering. Maximum arrival also depends on distributing input-dependent terms across 256 loaded outputs.",
  "rewrite": "Use two shared 4-to-16 active-low predecoders, followed by a two-input NOR function for each output. Each predecode term feeds 16 outputs. This exposes a shallow NAND-style predecode/NOR-style output topology instead of a variable shift.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to reduce maximum data arrival by reducing decode depth and sharing intermediate terms. The actual gain and slew/capacitance compliance require the specified mapping and STA flow; no measured result is claimed.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The design exposes 32 shared four-bit comparison terms and 256 two-input output combinations, plus input inversion and mapping-dependent buffers. Sharing should reduce duplicated decode logic, but the area cap and electrical limits remain to be verified after mapping.",
  "functional_boundaries": "For N=8, output k is asserted exactly when in[7:4] equals k/16 and in[3:0] equals k%16, equivalent to the original 256-bit one-hot shift for every binary input. Module name, ports, widths, unsigned declarations, and parameter declaration/default are preserved. Other parameter values retain the original expression. There is no storage, latency, assumption, or undefined output."
}
